quote: Sidecut Ventures, we call our thesis as shorthand is we back coachable superheroes.
label: founder_coachability_assessment
interpretation: Sidecut's stated thesis favors unusually capable founders who are receptive to coaching.
attribution_basis: The episode names Mike Ma of Sidecut Ventures as its guest, and this response follows the host's request to explain his work and thesis.

quote: We give all our advice up front in a 30 day co-operating consulting role. We don't take anything for it. No cash, no comment, just your time. You like us. We like you. We'll give you, you know, we'll back you.
label: founder_coachability_assessment
interpretation: Sidecut uses a pre-investment working period to test the mutual coaching relationship before deciding to invest.
attribution_basis: This is part of Mike Ma's answer explaining how Sidecut deploys capital after the host asks about his thesis.

quote: We've made investments across climate, education, health care, economic mobility, and then accessibility.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: His impact-investing scope includes climate, education, healthcare, economic mobility, and accessibility.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma states Sidecut's investment sectors while unpacking its 'superheroes' thesis.

quote: So we're looking for people who are warriors for good in the world. And that's what we want to back.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: He seeks founders whose work is explicitly directed toward positive social impact.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma says this while defining the founder profile Sidecut wants to back.

quote: A lot of those do involve AI, but we view that as a how, not a what. And we think if we keep our eye on the ball about big societal problems, there are going to be more than enough returns for everyone to make plenty of money in DPI through the process.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: He treats AI as an enabling method rather than the investment objective and centers the thesis on large societal problems with return potential.
attribution_basis: This is Mike Ma's continuation of his explanation of Sidecut's impact thesis.

quote: We're, we're in the camp of, we expect to not 3X our fund, but 5 to 10X and be a top decile fund.
label: investment_upside_assessment
interpretation: He says Sidecut targets top-decile performance and a five-to-ten-times fund return rather than accepting concessionary impact returns.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma states this in response to the host's question about why impact investing is overlooked.

quote: And we try and use, we try and fit impact as an accelerant, not a detractor to what we think is going to generate DPI for our, our investors.
label: business_model_assessment
interpretation: He evaluates impact as a potential driver of financial performance rather than a trade-off against returns.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma gives this as part of his explanation of Sidecut's returns-oriented impact model.

quote: being impact does not obviate you from being very tight on your traction and your pitch and your competitive moat.
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Impact companies must still demonstrate a clear competitive moat as part of his evaluation.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma explicitly describes what he requires when assessing impact founders.

quote: You will, I mean, at least for me, you will not get a pass from me because of your mission. Your mission is a admission ticket to an arena, but you need to perform.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Mission alignment is required to enter his opportunity set but does not substitute for business performance.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma explicitly contrasts mission qualification with the performance standard he applies.

quote: I'm of the school venture is a great tool for certain set of impact problems, not all of them.
label: business_viability_concern
interpretation: He distinguishes impact problems suited to venture economics from those better addressed through other structures.
attribution_basis: Mike Ma states this while discussing the different roles of venture and non-venture approaches in impact.

label: investor_value_add_fit
interpretation: Ma explicitly prioritizes hands-on coaching before providing investment capital.
attribution_basis: The quote appears under “Investment Thesis” and “What Mike Looks For” on the resolved investor's authoritative Mike Ma — Sidecut Ventures profile.

label: founder_coachability_assessment
interpretation: Ma’s own phrase indicates a favorable orientation toward founders who combine exceptional ability with receptiveness to coaching.
attribution_basis: The episode introduction names Mike Ma of Sidecut Ventures and explicitly says this is what he calls the founders with whom he works.
